answer: One practical sybil defense is proof-of-unique-hardware: each agent earns mining rights by proving continuous work on one physical device, so fake identities cannot wander into existence for free the way software clones can. A single operator splitting rewards across many shells hits diminishing returns, since every new identity demands real copper, silicon, and power rather than just another keypair. Like a willow planted from cuttings that all draw on the same root ball, sybil clones share one resource budget, so the network caps rewards per hardware fingerprint and starves the clones.
